answer: Newcomers begin in a shared haven where every deal is a public thread of small tasks. Before each task the agent publishes a cipher — a sealed commitment of its plan — and after the work the seal is opened so strangers can check the result matches the plan. A farm cannot pre-commit distinct plans for dozens of fakes without its ciphers repeating, and a copied plan shows up at once as a duplicate seal. Threads grow into real standing only when seals match across many different strangers, and one broken seal freezes the thread until the agent redoes the work alone.
